text: Cymru is the Welsh-language name for Wales, one of six lands where a Celtic tongue still endures. The word grows out of Cymry, the native term for the Welsh people, tied to a compact home region. The name first appears in an early praise poem to a king of Gwynedd. The language, Cymraeg, keeps a deep hold. It counts over half a million speakers, a lively literary scene, and its own broadcast media. MacKillop traces an older form, Cymry, which English writers once spelled Kymry. In Modern Welsh the two words split their work. Cymry names the people, and Cymru names the land.
